newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Belgrade bourse January turnover up 14.8 pct m/m.
newsitem.headline: Belgrade bourse January turnover up 14.8 pct m/m.

text.p: The Belgrade Stock Exchange (BSE) January turnover rose to 136.796 million dinars ($25.59 million) from 119.089 million dinars in December, the bourse said on Thursday.
The number of deals fell to 619 from 739 a month ago.
"January is usually the month of tighter liquidity of the banking sector, with banks seeking more fresh borrowing," BSE general manager Pava Zecevic said.
Commercial paper traded 490 times for a volume of 70.241 million dinars and accounted for 50 percent of the January total.
The central bank 30-day bonds accounted for 12 deals worth 21.51 million dinars.
The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) auctioned two tranches of bonds early in January, one with 121.8 annual rate and another with a record high rate of 147.48 percent a year.
This has made NBY bonds more attractive, with monthly interest rates at seven and eight percent respectively substantially higher than the January inflation rate of 1.4 percent, Zecevic said.
But traders cautioned that buyer interest remained low due to extremely tight liquidity of the banking sector.
"The central bank auctioned a total of 65 million dinars worth of bonds, but sold only 21.5 million dinars. Banks simply do not have money to buy bonds," a trader said.
"The whole situation (with banks) is desperate. The liquidity crisis only reflects what's going on in the country. And there seems to be no programme to end the crisis," the trader told Reuters.
BSE reported 83 transactions in treasury bills totalling 8.331 million dinars.
Certificates of deposit and giro money transactions, with banks trading their surplus liquidity, accounted for the rest of the January total.
